subject.title: fix(memory-core): honor private-network settings for OpenAI-compatible embeddings

question: Should OpenAI-compatible memory embeddings inherit `models.providers.<id>.request.allowPrivateNetwork` as their private-network trust boundary?
rationale: The code path is clear and the patch is focused, but the remaining choice is a security and upgrade contract decision rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Accept provider-policy inheritance
options.body: Land this PR's approach so memory embeddings reuse the existing configured provider transport trust policy with omitted/false/true coverage.

options.title: Require memory-specific policy
options.body: Reject or revise this PR in favor of a separate memory-scoped trust knob if maintainers want provider request policy to stay outside memory embeddings.

options.title: Keep default blocking only
options.body: Close the linked issue and keep private OpenAI-compatible memory endpoints behind external operator workarounds such as proxies.

recommendation.title: Accept provider-policy inheritance
recommendation.body: Land this PR's approach so memory embeddings reuse the existing configured provider transport trust policy with omitted/false/true coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to the merged OpenAI-compatible embedding provider and memory generic-provider bridge, so they are the best available owner for the memory/provider boundary choice.
